newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran commissions Tabriz petrochemical plant.
newsitem.headline: Iran commissions Tabriz petrochemical plant.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Monday officially commissioned Iran's new petrochemical plant in the northwestern city of Tabriz, the official news agency IRNA said.

It quoted Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh as saying the plant was built for $850 million in hard cash in addition to one trillion rials ($571 million) in local currency and would produce 400,000 tonnes of petrochemicals.

The output would include 136,000 tonnes of ethylene, 56,000 tonnes of propylene, 100,000 tonnes of polyethylene and 55,000 tonnes of benzene and a variety of aromatics, earlier reports said. The Tabriz plant came online in February.

Construction was also launched on Monday on new units at the plant which would produce 23,500 tonnes of SBR (styrene butadiene rubber) and 15,000 tonnes of SBL (styrene butadiene latex) per year as well as other petrochemicals, IRNA said.
Aghazadeh said Iran had exported $506 million worth of petrochemicals in the Iranian year that ended on March 20, the agency added.
Iran is the Middle East's second largest petrochemical producer after Saudi Arabia and aims to triple its annual output to 30 million tonnes in 25 years.

Under Iran's current five-year plan (1995-2000) the National Petrochemical Company (NPC) is to increase capacity to 15 million tonnes from the present 10 million tonnes with the construction of five new petrochemical plants. ($1=1,750 rials at the rate used for state budget accounts)
